feature: Ask says what it is doing while it works
summary: While Ask works on a request, its row in the Agent panel now carries one live line under the request saying what it is doing right now (getting the model ready, reading your request with how far through, writing the steps, planning, painting with how far through, turning it into layers, checking, trying again and why), with the time once a stage passes five seconds. The line goes when the request lands. An agent sees the same line in list_documents.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no flag changed from its default, built-in model and picture model set up in Settings > Ask.

try.do: Open an empty picture and press Command K.
Type: a fox in a forest at sunset, then press Return.
Watch the Agent group on the right: under the request, the grey line says Getting the model ready, then Reading your request with a rising percent.
Keep watching as it moves to Writing the steps, Planning, and Painting with its percent.
Watch it say Turning it into layers, then Checking it, and, when the check sees something else, Trying again with why (here: it looked like foxes).
Hover the line to read the whole of a line cut short.
When it lands, check the Agent group is still in view, the row says what it made and the live line is gone.

Play the reel 2026-11-01-ask-says-what-it-is-doing-reel-2.mp4 (the Agent group through a whole request, a frame every 2.5 s, ending on the finished row) or open the contact sheet 2026-11-01-ask-says-what-it-is-doing-sheet-2.png.

evaluate: Can you tell at a glance that it is moving and roughly how far along it is, at any moment of the request?
Is 'Reading your request, 41%' the right words for the minute the model spends taking in the request, or would you rather it said something else?
Is the grey line under the request quiet enough, or does it pull your eye while you work on the canvas?
Does the time on the right (10s, 1:05) help, or is the percent enough on its own?
rough: No mock covers a request at work: the Agent group mock (agent-generate-wt.html) shows only finished rows, so this goes further than the mock and removes nothing from it.

Five kinds of request measured at Next defaults (time, then the longest the line went without changing): the fox, 192 s, 15.0 s on Getting the model ready, which shows its time; the cat playing a guitar scene, 245 s, 12.5 s on Getting the model ready, shows its time; make the cat black (an edit to the picked drawing), 109 s, 9.5 s on Reading your request, 87%, shows its time; a photo of a dog on a beach, 166 s, 7.8 s; the component sheet, 242 to 269 s, 18.2 s and once 97.2 s on Writing the steps, which shows its time.

The sheet's 97 seconds on Writing the steps with only a clock is the weak spot: the model writes the whole plan in one answer and the app only learns the steps when it ends. Naming each step as it is written is task while-ask-writes-a-long-plan-its-line-names-each.

'Reading your request' is the model taking in everything sent with the request (about 15,000 tokens of instructions, tools and the document). Its percent is against Ask's own estimate of that size, because the model's server never says the whole; it is held under 100% and has finished between 87% and 97% so far. It now starts at 3%, no longer at the previous request's count first.

An edit to a picked layer reads its whole request twice (once more after it looks at the layers), so its percent climbs to about 90%, starts again at about 76% and climbs again. Honest, but can look like going backwards.

The Agent group now stays in view while a drawing is checked and when it lands (frames 136 s to finished in the new sheet). In one frame, as a 120 layer drawing landed, the line was blank for a moment while the canvas had not drawn yet either; the row kept its height.

Right after a component sheet lands the probe held for up to 466 ms and the Layers list and Agent rows drew a second late, which is what failed the rotating check's run of the sheet. Whether a person sees it outside the probe is task find-out-whether-landing-a-component-sheet-holds.
Long subjects are cut to fit the panel's 40 character line, keeping the part and percent ('Painting a fox in a forest at…, 33%'); the whole line is on the tooltip and in list_documents.
